chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about a man who owes me money and repays me with some dinars and some dirhams; when he comes to settle the account and pay me in full, the price of the dinars has changed. Which of the two prices do I calculate for him: the price that was on the day he gave me the dinars, or the price of the day I am settling with him? He said: 'The price of the day he gave you the dinars, because you withheld their benefit from him.'
ai.seo_question: How to calculate debt repayment when currency exchange rates change?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'holding the benefit' (*habas al-manfa'a*) to determine debt valuation during currency fluctuation. By ruling that repayment is based on the original exchange rate, the Imam emphasizes that the debtor bears the risk of delay, as they effectively retained the utility of the specific dinars during the interim period. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential focus on fairness in financial transactions, ensuring the creditor is not disadvantaged by the debtor's retention of funds.
